line: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 cxd5 Nb8 Bc4
teaches: In the structures that come from this pawn grab, the question is always the square in front of the queen's pawn — the shortest way to judge these positions is to ask who controls that square. Hold what you have won with pieces, not more pawn moves, and make the opponent prove the pawn comes back.
explains: The bishop develops to c4 and defends the pawn on d5 — the extra pawn the whole line revolves around. As long as it stands there, the opponent's pieces are tied to regaining it, which means every developing move that holds it is a move that also cramps them.
